name: Southwest Florida International Airport
before:
The airport for the whole south west Florida coast, taking in Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Naples, Marco Island and Punta Gorda. It is ten miles south east of Fort Myers and a United States customs port of entry.

It does all that on one runway. At 12,000 feet it is a long one, and the airport is now the second busiest single runway airport in the country after San Diego, handling 11,154,458 passengers in 2025, its highest ever. Studies for a second runway are under way.

The terminal covers 798,000 square feet with 28 gates across three concourses and is designed for ten million passengers a year, so it is already running beyond that. It can be built out to 65 gates across five concourses. Parking is generous at 11,250 spaces, with a separate three storey structure for short stays.

Of the 13,555 acre site, around 6,000 acres are conserved swamp land set aside for environmental mitigation.
after:
The main commercial airport for the Fort Myers area of south west Florida, and for Naples and Marco Island too. It is ten miles south east of Fort Myers and has US customs for international flights.

In 2025 it handled 11,154,458 passengers, the most in its history. All of that traffic runs on one runway, 12,000 feet long, on a site of 13,555 acres.

claims.claim: the main commercial airport for the Fort Myers area of south west Florida
claims.inAfter: The main commercial airport for the Fort Myers area of south west Florida
claims.note: Was 'The airport for the whole south west Florida coast'. Lee County's visitor bureau (a county department) uses the words 'main commercial airport for the Fort Myers area'. The FAA's 2025 table shows other airports with scheduled flights on the same coast (Punta Gorda 1,140,842 boardings, Sarasota/Bradenton 2,242,138), so 'the whole coast' is dropped.

claims.inAfter: has US customs for international flights
claims.note: Was 'a United States customs port of entry'. The FAA data (as printed by AirNav, effective 3 September 2026) class it as a customs landing rights airport and a customs user fee airport, where CBP clears international arrivals at the airport's cost; a user fee airport is not the same thing as a designated port of entry, so the text now says only that it has customs for international flights. Wikipedia puts the customs hall on the lower level of Concourse B. CBP's own port pages could not be found (its Florida list answered 404).

Customs and Immigration services for international flights are located on the lower level of Concourse B.

claims.claim: the airport for the whole south west Florida coast
claims.wasBefore: The airport for the whole south west Florida coast
claims.why: Overstated: Punta Gorda (1,140,842 boardings in 2025) and Sarasota/Bradenton (2,242,138) have their own airports with scheduled flights on the same coast (FAA). Reworded to the Fort Myers area, plus Naples and Marco Island, each with two sources.

claims.claim: taking in Cape Coral and Punta Gorda
claims.wasBefore: taking in Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Naples, Marco Island and Punta Gorda
claims.why: Cape Coral and Punta Gorda rest on Wikipedia's metro-area list alone (the operator's sites could not be read), and Punta Gorda has its own airport. Fort Myers, Naples and Marco Island are kept.

claims.claim: a United States customs port of entry
claims.wasBefore: a United States customs port of entry
claims.why: The FAA data class it as a customs landing rights and user fee airport, not a port of entry; CBP's port pages could not be found. Softened to customs for international flights (see above).

claims.claim: at 12,000 feet it is a long one
claims.wasBefore: At 12,000 feet it is a long one
claims.why: The length is kept with three sources; 'a long one' is dropped as a judgement.

claims.claim: second busiest single runway airport in the US after San Diego
claims.wasBefore: the airport is now the second busiest single runway airport in the country after San Diego
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and its cited source is a 2015 San Diego article. The operator's sites (flylcpa.com and flyrsw.com) answer with a Cloudflare bot check and are treated as blocked, so the airport's own wording could not be read.

claims.claim: studies for a second runway are under way
claims.wasBefore: Studies for a second runway are under way.
claims.why: Wikipedia contradicts itself (a parallel runway 'under development', 'delayed indefinitely' and 'studies ... underway'), and the only other source, the Florida DOT's undated facility sheet with 2023 figures, says only 'a future parallel runway'. Nothing dated within 12 months could be read; the operator's projects page answers with a Cloudflare bot check (blocked).

claims.claim: terminal of 798,000 square feet with 28 gates across three concourses
claims.wasBefore: The terminal covers 798,000 square feet with 28 gates across three concourses
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and it contradicts itself (28 gates in one section, 27 in another). The terminal is also changing: Construction Dive (24 March 2025) reported the start of a 14-gate Concourse E due in 2027, but nothing dated within 12 months confirms its progress.

claims.claim: designed for ten million passengers a year, already beyond it
claims.wasBefore: and is designed for ten million passengers a year, so it is already running beyond that
claims.why: The design capacity rests on Wikipedia's facilities list alone.

claims.claim: can be built out to 65 gates across five concourses
claims.wasBefore: It can be built out to 65 gates across five concourses.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; an old planning figure, overtaken by the Concourse E project.

claims.claim: 11,250 parking spaces and a three storey short-stay structure
claims.wasBefore: Parking is generous at 11,250 spaces, with a separate three storey structure for short stays.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the operator's sites answer with a Cloudflare bot check (blocked).

claims.claim: around 6,000 acres of conserved swamp for environmental mitigation
claims.wasBefore: around 6,000 acres are conserved swamp land set aside for environmental mitigation
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The site's 13,555 acres are kept (FAA record).
